6800.full: Tartarus , a dark abyss, as deep below Hades as earth below heaven, the prison of the Titans, (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—;later, the nether world , like Ἅιδης, (Hesiod) derivation uncertain (ML)

6801.full: Τίτος, -ου, ὁ Titus; __1. St. Paul's disciple and companion: 2Co.2:13 7:6 7:13-14 8:6 8:16 8:23 12:18, Gal.2:1, 3, 2Ti.4:10, Tit.1:4, subscr., Rec. (Τῖτος). __2. One surnamed Justus: Act.18:7, RV (T, WH, Τίτιος).† (AS)

6802.full: Φαγωρ Phagor - a name found only in LXX at Jos.15.59 with no equivalent in the Hebrew text

6806.full: Φάλεκ (T, Rec. Φαλέκ, L, mg., Φάλεγ), ὁ indecl. (Heb. D, Ge 1116), Peleg: Luk.3:35.† (AS)

6812.full: αἰγιαλός, -οῦ, ὁ (on the derivation, see Boisacq, see word), [in LXX: Jdg.5:17 (חוֹף), Sir.24:14 * ;] the sea-shore, beach (cf. Field, Notes, 146; DCG, i, 175 f.; MM, VGT, see word): Mat.13:2,48 Jhn.21:4, Act.21:5 27:39,40.† (AS)

6816.full: 1. a herd of goats , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 2. a goat-pasture , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

s: to lose blood, suffer from a flow of blood
6819.full: αἱμορροέω, (αἷμα, ῥέω), [in LXX: Lev.15:33 (דָּוֶה) * ;] to lose blood, suffer from a flow of blood (Hipp.): Mat.9:20.† (AS)

s: to smite so as to make bloody
to welter in blood, be slain
6820.full: to make bloody stain with blood , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;hence to smite so as to make bloody , (Sophocles Tragicus); so in Mid., [variant datesAnthology Palantina:—;Pass. to welter in blood, be slain , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

s: to play on a flute, to pipe
6830.full: αὐλέω, -ῶ (αὐλός), [in Al.: 3Ki.1:40 * ;] to play on a flute, to pipe: mid., Mat.11:17, Luk.7:32, 1Co.14:7.† (AS)

6832.full: αὐστηρός, -ά, -όν (αἄω, to dry up) [in LXX: 2Ma.14:30 * ;] prop., stringent, harsh to the taste. Metaphorical, in Inscr., of a rough country; of disposition and manners, strict, severe (as in π., of an inspector; MM, s v): Luk.19:21-22.† SYN.: σκληρός (Tr., § xiv) (AS)

s: in close fight, in the fray
6835.full: 1. hand to hand , αὐτοσχεδίηι (i.e. μάχηι) in close fight, in the fray , (Iliad by Homer): αὐτοσχεδίην as adverb, = αὐτοσχεδόν, (Homer) 2. off-hand , of an improvisatore, (Homeric Hymns) (ML)

6836.full: 1. drought , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. the effects of drought, squalor , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

6847.full: βαρέω, -ῶ (later form of βαρύνω, which see), [in LXX: Exo.7:14 (כָּבֵד), 2Ma.13:9 * ;] to depress, weigh down. In NT, in pass. only: Mat.26:43, Luk.9:32 21:34, 2Co.1:8 5:4, 1Ti.5:16.† (AS)

s: the seats next the orchestra, reserved for the Council
6860.full: 1. of or for the council or the councillors , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. able to advise or deliberate , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 3. as Substantive, βουλευτικόν, in the Athen. theatre, the seats next the orchestra, reserved for the Council , (Aristophanes Comicus) 4. the senatorial order , (Plutarch) (ML)

6864.full: βραβεύω (βραβεύς, an umpire), [in LXX: Wis.10:12 * ;] __(a) prop., to act as umpire; hence, __(b) generally, to arbitrate, decide (Isocr., Dem.; Lft., Col., l.with; MM, see word): Col.3:15; __(with) in some late writers, to direct, rule, control (so in Col., l.with, accusative to Thayer, see word, Meyer, in l.), (cf. κατα-βραβεύω). † (AS)

s: to cause to sink, to sink
6869.full: βυθίζω (βυθός), [in LXX: 2Ma.12:4 * ;] trans., to cause to sink, to sink: metaphorically, εἰς ὄλεθρον, 1Ti.6:9; pass., to sink, intrans.: Luk.5:7.† (AS)

6870.full: 1. a gulf, pit :—; at Athens a cleft behind the Acropolis, into which criminals were thrown, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. metaphorically ruin, perdition , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

6871.lxx: in LXX: Tob.13:17 (-ύλλιον in Exo.28:20, שֹׁהַם *
6871.full: βήρυλλος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ, [in LXX: Tob.13:17 (-ύλλιον in Exo.28:20, שֹׁהַם * ;]) beryl, a jewel of sea-green colour: Rev.21:20.† (AS)

6872.full: βίωσις, -εως, ἡ (βιόω), [in LXX: Si prol. 12 * ;] manner of life: Act.26:4.† (AS)

6874.full: 1. to stuff , 2. with genitive rei, to stuff full of , only in Pass., νήματος βεβυσμένος stuffed full of spun-work or yarn, (Odyssey by Homer); τὸ στόμα ἐβέβυστο [i.e. χρυσοῦ] (Herdotus Historicus) 3. with dative rei, to stop or bung up with, plug : Pass., σπογγίωι βεβυσμένος (Aristophanes Comicus) 4. absolute, βεβ. τὰ ὦτα deaf , (Lucian) (ML)

6893.full: γενέσια, -ων, τά, neut. pl. of adj. -ιος, -ον, relating to birth (γένεσις); __1. in Attic Gk., a commemoration of the dead. __2. In late Gk., a birthday feast (= cl. γενέθλια; so in π., see MM, Exp., x; cf. also Ῥutherford, NPhr., 184): Mat.14:6, Mrk.6:21. † (AS)

6894.full: γενεαλογέω, -ῶ (γενεά, λέγω), [in LXX: 1Ch.5:1 (יחשׁ)* ;] to trace ancestry, reckon genealogy; pass., before ἐκ: Heb.7:6.† (AS)
